description: Email notification system using Resend or SendGrid to send transactional emails on key events. Creates email service wrapper, adds email templates (already exist in lib/email-templates.ts), triggers emails from API routes (signup, OTP, proposal, payment, delivery), and adds email preferences UI. Independent of FEAT-001 (in-app notifications) but complements it.
steps: 1. Choose email provider: Resend (recommended, simpler API) or SendGrid. Install dependency: npm install resend OR npm install @sendgrid/mail. Add RESEND_API_KEY or SENDGRID_API_KEY to .env.local. Document in README.

2. Create lib/email.ts email service wrapper: export async function sendEmail({ to, subject, html }). Use Resend or SendGrid client. Handle errors gracefully (log error, don't throw - email failures shouldn't break API calls). Add retry logic for transient failures (3 retries with exponential backoff).

3. Review existing templates in lib/email-templates.ts: generateWelcomeEmail(name, loginUrl), generateOTPEmail(code, email), generateProposalNotification(brandName, creatorName, briefTitle, proposalUrl), generateBriefMatchEmail(creatorName, briefTitle, matchScore, briefUrl). Verify HTML is well-formed and mobile-responsive.
4. Add email trigger to app/api/auth/signup/route.ts (if not exists, create it): after successful signup, call sendEmail with generateWelcomeEmail template. Include link to /dashboard.

5. Add email trigger to app/api/auth/otp/route.ts (if not exists, create it): when OTP requested, call sendEmail with generateOTPEmail template. OTP should be stored in database (see FEAT-004 for persistent OTP storage).

6. Add email trigger to app/api/proposals/route.ts POST endpoint: after proposal inserted, fetch brand email from brand_profiles join users, call sendEmail with generateProposalNotification template. Include link to /briefs/[id].

7. Add email trigger to app/api/proposals/route.ts PATCH endpoint (proposal accepted): fetch creator email, call sendEmail with subject 'Your proposal was accepted!', body with brief title and link to /projects/[agreementId].
8. Add email trigger to app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts payment_intent.succeeded handler: fetch creator email, call sendEmail with subject 'Payment received', body with amount and project link.

9. Add email trigger to app/api/deliveries/route.ts POST endpoint: after delivery uploaded, fetch brand email, call sendEmail with subject 'New delivery uploaded', body with project title and link to review delivery.

10. Create database/migrations/012_email_preferences.sql: add email_preferences JSONB column to users table with default { proposal_submitted: true, proposal_accepted: true, payment_received: true, delivery_uploaded: true, review_submitted: true, message_received: true }. Users can opt-out of individual email types.

11. Create app/api/settings/email-preferences/route.ts: GET endpoint returns user's email_preferences JSONB. PATCH endpoint updates preferences (merge with existing, don't replace entirely). Verify auth session.

12. Create app/settings/email/page.tsx: UI with checkboxes for each email type (In-App + Email columns). Fetch preferences on mount, update via PATCH /api/settings/email-preferences. Show success toast on save. Match existing settings page style.
13. Update email sending logic in lib/email.ts: before sending, check user's email_preferences. If user has opted out of that email type, skip sending (log skipped email for debugging).

📝 NOTES:
- OTP email route: No dedicated OTP request route exists. OTP verification is handled by Supabase Auth's built-in system. The sendOTPEmail function is ready for integration if a custom OTP flow is implemented later.
- Email templates: Used inline HTML templates in lib/email.ts instead of reading from emails/*.html files (the lib/email-templates.ts file exists but uses filesystem reads which don't work in serverless). Inline templates are mobile-responsive and match the design.
- Service client: Used createServiceClient() from lib/supabase.ts for server-side email preference lookups to bypass RLS.

3. Test emails by triggering events (signup, proposals, etc.)
